purpose: Pass-1 source curation after actual body read; not independent question verification

evidence.summary: Connects through the root CosmosClient; recommends application-lifetime client reuse, distinguishes lightweight database/container handles, point reads and queries, and create/upsert/replace item operations. Do not use the illustrative if_match snippet or expand account-key security assertions.
Documents separate name/value query parameters, partition routing, projection, page size and lazy iteration, array queries, and request-charge observation. No latency or RU number is guaranteed.

Documents array-valued embeddings; immutable path/type/dimension/metric policies at container creation; float32, float16, int8 and uint8; vector-index types and minimum effective index population. Preserves corrected float16 support but excludes universal negligible-loss or whole-database 50-percent savings claims. Cosine scoring inconsistencies are excluded.

Documents VectorDistance query shape, TOP, projection, same-model query embeddings, and explicit brute-force option. The prose cosine-similarity direction conflicts with default ascending examples; no candidate relies on that scoring interpretation.

Combines metadata eligibility with vector queries and explicitly targets the partition key. Optimizer-dependent pre/post filtering is not a universal exhaustive-recall or exact result-count guarantee. Hybrid full-text/RRF implementation is not used in this batch.

Explains lease checkpoint/ownership/failover, push versus scheduled pull processing, selective content-hash-based refresh, and updating the embedding and content hash together. Excludes exactly-once wording, illustrative always-true refresh code, unsupported standalone runtime tables, and malformed pull start flags.

Documents property order and full-direction reversal for composite ORDER BY, equality-first/range-last composite filtering, per-write index costs, and asynchronous add-before-remove index transformation. No nested-path specificity rule is inferred beyond the actual examples.

Distinguishes exact flat, quantizedFlat and diskANN; 505-dimensional flat limit, 1000-vector effective-index threshold, separation from range indexing, and immutable vector policies. Optional tuning feature-release assertions and generalized prefilter guarantees are excluded.

Relates write costs to indexed paths and actual filter/sort workloads; compares retrieved/output metrics, selective indexing, and asynchronous transformations. Benchmark results must be interpreted for measured data rather than universal cost promises.

Documents partition-bound session tokens and explicit handoff between SDK clients, read-your-writes versus weaker consistency, and relative read RU costs. Does not license strengthening an account default per request or promise instant ANN indexing.

Documents issued Entra token strings as database passwords, PostgreSQL token resource, native authentication, TLS verification modes, and direct 5432 versus enabled General Purpose/Memory Optimized PgBouncer 6432 endpoints. No username-format generalization is used.

Documents typed columns, JSONB, BYTEA, NOT NULL/UNIQUE/foreign keys, composite keys, and table/index separation. Excludes the incorrect claim that RESTRICT is the default referential action and absolute trailing-index-column limitations.
Documents JSONB extraction and containment, keyset pagination with a unique tie-breaker, RETURNING, and ON CONFLICT. The broad SELECT alias statement about GROUP BY/LIMIT is excluded.

Documents psycopg parameter tuples, result-fetch modes, connection/cursor context managers, connection and statement timeouts, transient versus syntax/constraint failures, COPY batching, and application pool checkout. External library sites are not admitted sources.

Documents installed vector extension, dimensioned vector columns, dense/half/sparse representations and distinct distance operators. No omitted extension allowlisting prerequisite or model-specific output guarantee is inferred.

Documents IVFFlat data-dependent clustering versus HNSW empty-table construction, runtime probes/search width, and metric/operator-class correspondence. Directly links the exact pgvector performance product article. Excludes universal latency/recall targets.

Documents index progress/usage monitoring, deferred stale-embedding refresh, parallel model columns, table/index sizing and MVCC old row versions. Excludes the invalid 3072-dimensional standard-vector HNSW example, erroneous migration-time arithmetic, and fixed index-size multipliers.

Documents metadata/index cost-based plan selection, evaluated distance thresholds plus count limits, content projections, multi-aspect and hybrid retrieval. Never assumes every ANN query physically prefilters or that a global threshold fits all corpora.

Documents source/chunk tables, adjacency, token budgets, provenance projections, version filters, and precision/recall evaluation. No flawed DISTINCT/window snippet is reused; citation usefulness does not establish probabilistic confidence.

Distinguishes shared_buffers, per-operation work_mem and nonallocating effective_cache_size; documents measured plans, CPU/memory/I/O and runtime search settings. Explicitly excludes the incorrect quadratic vector-distance dimension-scaling claim and integer-dividing cache-hit snippet.

Documents construction versus query parameters, empirical IVFFlat/HNSW tradeoffs and concurrent maintenance. Excludes universal timing, guaranteed recall and questionable dimensional/memory multipliers.

Documents metadata B-tree/GIN/expression indexes, partial indexes, typed-plus-flexible schemas, cost-based filtering and partition-aligned scans. Excludes universal filter ordering and absolute trailing-column or GIN-operator claims.

Documents actual CPU/memory/I/O driven vertical scaling, asynchronous read-only replicas with separate endpoints, primary routing for immediate reads and workload-dependent caching. Excludes fixed SKU ranges, universal thresholds, legacy Redis endpoints and discounts.

Documents transaction/session/statement pooling, borrowed connection contexts, transaction-local settings, bounded retry and per-instance pool budgets. Does not rely on blanket session reset guarantees, prepared-statement incompatibility or dated tier connection limits.

Documents OSS same-slot multi-key requirements, Enterprise command exceptions, cluster-capable clients, pipeline efficiency and SCAN rather than blocking KEYS. Does not use external Redis/GitHub links as technical citations.

Documents Redis string/hash/list/counter operations, atomic numeric increments, cache-aside invalidation, key-level TTL/EXPIRE/PERSIST and incremental SCAN. SETEX is specifically string-only despite a broad introductory sentence.

Documents index key prefixes, HASH binary vectors, dimension/type matching, KNN dialect 2 and EF_RUNTIME. Excludes pipeline atomicity generalization, unsupported absolute model-metric assertions and unbounded range-result-count claims.

Documents FLOAT32/FLOAT64 element widths and workload-tested precision tradeoffs, FLAT/HNSW differences and query-local EF_RUNTIME. No universal memory-total, latency, recall or metric suitability guarantee is used.

Documents flat HASH field/binary-vector storage versus RedisJSON nested documents/numeric-array vectors with matching index types. Excludes migration that overwrites an existing HASH key with JSON without removal and claims about exact JSON memory size.

Directly linked product reference distinguishes estimated versus measured EXPLAIN, fixed-dimension standard vector indexes, all-lists IVFFlat exact-search fallback, runtime versus build parameters and partial-index predicate matching. Excludes the SET-without-LOCAL transaction example and generalized modern alternative-type dimension limits.
